question: S5: throttling onset time vs ambient and its effect on deadlines
labels: VX-1 is a fictional SoC; every power and thermal parameter is an assumption (power/params_vx1.yaml).
Thermal design rule (assumption): enclosure sized so S1 P0 keeps the hottest junction at 85 C at a 40 C rated ambient, giving enclosure_to_ambient_r_k_per_w = 4.5.
Parts C and D compress slow thermal dynamics: package and enclosure heat capacity divided by 100. Onset times there are scenario seconds, not wall-clock minutes; part B gives physical-mass times.
Thermal settle: 1 s burn-in, then the thermal state jumps to the steady state for the measured power (to the 100 C throttle threshold if no steady state exists).
Parts A and B are model calculations on power measured in a co-sim run, not co-sim results.
Onset = first step where a thermal OPP cap is below the OPP the policy wanted (binding throttle).
